items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — jumped straight from the greeting to 'Is this a good time to talk about your move?'

No Save Your Ass prep speech at all — nothing about prep shortening the move, no consolidation examples (toys, drawers, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip. This is the biggest miss on a 3-bedroom, 8-9 hour move.
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000). Said only 'insurance' is included, with no explanation and no 60c/lb baseline.
Never mentioned Meet Your Mover (pre-move email with the mover's photo and info).
Never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee (discount if we miss the arrival window).
No 'Pricing is super simple' opener — went straight into 'let me discuss the pricing and the estimate here.'
Never explained the clock starts on-site when the contract opens — only gave the 2.5 hr minimum and 15-min increments.
No sense-check after the pricing/clock block ('Does that make sense?'). Customer only replied 'Mm-hmm' through a long run-on delivery.
Probe gaps: never asked about packing services, storage stops, additional stops, walk distance / narrow hallways / tight turns, or moving stressors ('anything you're particularly worried about?').
Walk distance never assessed even though she noted a sloping driveway at the origin — no school-bus equivalent used, and traffic was never named as a variable for the cross-town leg.
Email handoff incomplete — no mention of the bolded detail list at the top of the email and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask.
No business hours given at close; only 'reply to that email or give us a call.'
Used the customer's name only twice, and mispronounced it as 'Luisa' on the farewell. Defaulted to 'sir' throughout.
top_strength: The estimate build was genuinely well-reasoned: she anchored on a 6.5-8.5 hour typical range for a 1600 sqft home, then explicitly adjusted up to 8-9 hours because of the washer/dryer and fridge and the two-story destination, and named the movers, truck, and dollar range ($1,711-$1,903). She also opened with real value by steering Luis to Sunday for the discounted rate after Friday came back fully booked.
coaching_note: Jeline runs a clean, organized intake but skipped all three Einstein differentiators and the entire Save Your Ass speech on an 8-9 hour move. Add the prep speech and the No Worries / Meet Your Mover / On-Time Guarantee block — on a quote-shopping customer who explicitly said 'I'm trying to see what you all got,' those differentiators are the only thing separating Einstein from the price on the next call.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and professional but transactional — heavy 'sir,' almost no affirmations or empathy markers, no rapport moment, and the customer had to ask her to repeat a question twice.
